union_rule_bb_blocks.integrated_block_minus1: PASSES via the CPL+BB pair only (LRT_CPLBB_CPL = 104.92, kT = 32.55 keV, CPLBB_VALID = True); the Band+BB pair FAILS there (LRT = 5.10)
union_rule_bb_blocks.baseline_dependence: EXTREME and systematic - this burst is the sharpest instance of the T8/union-rule lesson in the campaign so far. Block-by-block LRT_BANDBB_BAND vs LRT_CPLBB_CPL: blk0 0.81 vs 21.41; blk3 16.37 vs 94.38; blk4 8.66 vs 121.09; blk5 5.01 vs 50.46; blk6 -0.00 vs 11.52; blk7 2.66 vs 12.84. A Band-baseline-only test would have counted 2 BB blocks; the CPL baseline counts 6. The published mechanism is stated verbatim by Burgess+2014 for THIS burst: 'the flexibility of the Band function can mask the need for the blackbody component ... The Band function makes up for these effects by having a harder alpha.' Our archival BAND_ALPHA is indeed very hard in exactly those blocks (+0.52, +0.50, +0.85, +0.66, +0.52, +0.32).
union_rule_bb_blocks.counter_case: blk2 is the mirror image: Band+BB fires (LRT = 10.65, kT = 2.35 keV) while CPL+BB does NOT (LRT = -0.00). Recorded so the union is not read as 'CPL+BB always wins'.

archival_prior.kT_track_note: The CPL+BB kT track (125 -> 57 -> 38 -> 28 -> 25 -> 26 keV over 0-8 s) tracks Li+2019's published kT (111.6 -> 79.3 -> 52.0 -> 34.4 -> [unconstrained] -> 16.3 -> 22.0 keV) closely in blocks 0, 3, 4 and 7 and disagrees badly in block 2. The Band+BB kT track does NOT (2.2-2.4 keV in blocks 1-2, then 45.5 keV in block 3) - a hallmark of the harder-alpha degeneracy.

predictions: P-A (Ep track, falsifiable): the fresh blind Ep(t) over [-2, 32] s is MONOTONICALLY hard-to-soft after the first ~0.4 s, with the earliest well-constrained block (t < 0.7 s) carrying Ep in 450-900 keV, the pulse-peak region (1.2-2.8 s) in 280-480 keV, ~180-260 keV by 3-4 s, 110-160 keV at 6-10 s, and <= 80 keV by 20 s. FALSIFIED if any well-constrained (S >= 20) block breaks monotonicity by more than its 1-sigma error, or if the first block's Ep < 300 keV, or if Ep at 6-10 s exceeds 250 keV. Envelope built from Yu+2019 Band Ep, Yu+2016 Table A.1 and Lu+2018 Table 2, all frame-aligned to nu-F-nu peak.

P-B (BB / union rule, falsifiable, THE decisive prediction): the L18+ engine fires the union rule ((LRT_BANDBB_BAND >= 9.2 & kT > 1.05) OR (LRT_CPLBB_CPL >= 9.2 & kT > 1.05)) in AT LEAST 5 of ~12 blocks, concentrated in 0 - 8 s, driven predominantly by the CPL+BB pair, with a kT that DECREASES monotonically from ~80-130 keV in the first second to ~20-40 keV by 5-8 s. FALSIFIED if (a) the union tally is 0 or 1 - which would contradict Burgess+2014, Li+2019, Li+2020, Iyyani+2016 AND Acuner+2020's P = 1.00 simultaneously and would be the strongest negative reconciliation result in the campaign, or (b) kT RISES with time, or (c) the Band+BB pair alone drives the tally with CPL+BB silent (the reverse of the archival baseline dependence). NOTE the prior: this burst is the most strongly primed photospheric burst we have touched - a positive BB here is weak confirmation, a negative is highly informative.

P-B2 (baseline dependence, falsifiable): in at least 3 blocks the two nested tests DISAGREE at the 9.2 threshold (one fires, the other does not), and the disagreement is systematically in the direction CPL+BB > Band+BB in the hard blocks where BAND_ALPHA > +0.3. FALSIFIED if the two tests agree block-for-block, or if the disagreement runs the other way in the hard blocks. This is the direct, quantitative test of Burgess+2014's stated mechanism ('the Band function makes up for these effects by having a harder alpha') and is the reason the union rule exists.

P-C (two-break, falsifiable, with an L8 seed guard): at most a HANDFUL of blocks show DSBPL preference, and the only candidate that survives a break-location screen sits in the rise/peak, 0.67-2.22 s, with a lower break XB in 100-250 keV. FALSIFIED as a real two-break detection if every DSBPL win in the fresh run places XB below ~25 keV (the NaI low-energy rail: 7 of the 12 archival blocks do exactly that, XB = 11-21 keV) - such wins are engine artifacts, not breaks. Corroborating external evidence for genuine break structure exists and is INDEPENDENT of our engine: Yu+2016 selected SBPL as the best model in 7 of the first 26 bins of this burst (bins 2-4, 6-7, 11, 13, 24, 26), so a fresh SBPL/DSBPL preference in the 0.7-4 s range would reproduce a published, non-Fermi-team model selection.

P-D (hardness / synchrotron limit, falsifiable): the blind low-energy index exceeds -2/3 in >= 60% of well-constrained blocks and exceeds 0 in >= 4 blocks. FALSIFIED if fewer than 40% of blocks exceed -2/3. Anchors: Basak&Rao 2014 mean alpha = +0.013 +/- 0.017 with 16/18 bins above the line; Li+2026 f_-2/3 = 0.69; Acuner+2020 alpha_CPL = +0.27 +/- 0.03; Yu+2019 Band alpha positive in 8 of its first 9 bins.

P-E (frame trap, procedural, non-falsifiable but binding): NO Ep diff may be run before aligning (i) interval - our [-2, 32] s vs the catalog/GCN [-0.064, +83.0] s vs Konus [0, 102.1] s vs Suzaku [-0.5, +18.5] s; (ii) convention - Li+2019 report Ec (e-folding, Ep = (2+alpha)Ec), Yu+2016 report Ep AND Eb and warn verbatim 'we should not compare the Band function's Ep or Ec to the smoothly broken power law's Eb'; (iii) the dilution scale on THIS burst, published by Preece+2016: Ep,peak = 597 +/- 63 keV vs Ep,fluence = 239 +/- 10 keV, a factor 2.5. Our archival integrated-block Band Ep = 227.7 keV over [-0.05, 32] s already sits BELOW the GCN's 283 +/- 7 keV over [-0.064, 83] s - a difference in the counter-intuitive direction that must be explained by model and detector set, not waved through.

P-F (duration / component coverage, procedural): the fresh run must NOT be diffed against 'the' T90. The published values span 12 s (Suzaku, 100-1000 keV, main peak) to ~100 s (Konus, 20 keV-2 MeV), with Qin+2013 giving 15.55 s in 8-1000 keV against the GBM catalog's 81.79 s in 50-300 keV - a factor ~6 in nearly the same band that is METHOD, not energy. Our window covers the entire T50.

literature_BB_claims: PRESENT AND UNANIMOUS - the opposite of a null-streak burst. Burgess+2014 (bright BB, F_BB/F_syn = 0.5), Li+2019 (11 bins, all dDIC favour BB), Li+2020 (hybrid jet), Iyyani+2016 (Gamma > 1000 from that BB), Acuner+2020 (photosphere P = 1.00, ln Z ratio 1013). No paper argues against a thermal component in this burst.
literature_two_break_claims: NONE explicitly. The nearest external evidence is Yu+2016's per-bin model selection, where SBPL (a broken power law) beats BAND/COMP/PL in 7 of the first 26 bins. Iyyani+2016's 'two breaks are consistent' refers to breaks in the TIME evolution of E_sync and T, not to spectral breaks - do not conflate.
